figures.caption: Figure 4. Overview of the slide encoder training stages. Blue arrows denote Stage 1 pretraining, while red arrows indicate Stage 2. In Stage 1, randomly masked tiles are processed by the hybrid encoder without pruning, and a lightweight MAE decoder reconstructs the masked tokens. In Stage 2, masking and the decoder are removed and the pruner is trained using CLIP-based text-slide alignment objectives.

Figure 1. Overview of SLICEChat. Patch embeddings of the WSI are created by encoding the tiles with the CONCH v1.5 patch encoder. These patch embeddings are then transformed and pruned in the hybrid state-space slide encoder. The pruner uses learned queries to score and progressively select informative slide tokens. We use a LLaVA-style multimodal fusion to pass the pruned slide tokens to the MLLM.
